findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the EC2 user_data script, which is visible to anyone with instance metadata access or console/API describe permissions, leading to credential compromise.

The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (and the setting is explicitly commented out), leaving data at rest unencrypted and increasing risk of data exposure if the underlying storage is compromised or snapshots are shared.
The EBS snapshot inherits from an unencrypted source volume and has no encryption configured, so snapshot data (and any copies/shares) remain unencrypted at rest.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management interface of the instance to the entire internet.

The security group allows inbound TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 directly to the instance with no load balancer or other intermediary in this configuration, broadening the attack surface directly to the instance.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to instances in this subnet, and combined with the permissive security group allowing 0.0.0.0/0 on ports 22/80, this directly exposes the web host to the internet.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, risking unauthorized access to sensitive network traffic metadata.
